issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), Ministry of Public Security (MPS), and State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
covered_actors: Algorithm recommendation service providers providing internet information services within the People's Republic of China
Algorithm recommendation service providers with public opinion attributes or social mobilization capabilities
Algorithm recommendation service providers offering internet news information services
Algorithm recommendation service providers serving minors, the elderly, workers (work dispatch services), and consumers
Relevant industry organizations (encouraged to strengthen self-regulation)
Institutions and personnel participating in security assessment and supervision/inspection
prohibited_practices: Using algorithm recommendation services to endanger national security or public interest, disrupt economic or social order, or infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of others (Art. 6)
Using algorithm recommendation services to disseminate information prohibited by laws and administrative regulations (Art. 6)
Setting algorithm models that violate laws, regulations, or ethics, such as inducing user addiction or excessive consumption (Art. 8)
Recording keywords of illegal or harmful information into user interest points or user tags to push information (Art. 10)
Generating or synthesizing fake news information, or disseminating news published by entities outside the state-prescribed scope (Art. 13)
Using algorithms to falsely register accounts, illegally trade accounts, manipulate user accounts, or fabricate likes, comments, or reposts (Art. 14)

Using algorithms to block information, over-recommend, manipulate rankings or search results, or control hot searches or featured selections to interfere with information presentation, influence online public opinion, or evade supervision (Art. 14)
Using algorithms to impose unreasonable restrictions on other internet information service providers or obstruct their normal operations to engage in monopoly or unfair competition (Art. 15)
Pushing information to minors that may induce imitation of unsafe or socially immoral behaviors, induce bad habits, harm physical or mental health, or induce internet addiction (Art. 18)
Implementing unreasonable differential treatment in transaction conditions such as pricing based on consumer preferences, transaction habits, or other characteristics (Art. 21)
enforcement_authorities: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) and local cyberspace administration departments
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and local telecommunications departments
Ministry of Public Security (MPS) and local public security departments
State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local market regulation departments
compliance_deadlines: Within 10 working days of commencing service: Providers with public opinion attributes or social mobilization capabilities must complete algorithm filing (Art. 24)
Within 10 working days of any change: Providers must file updates to changed registration information (Art. 24)
Within 20 working days of terminating service: Providers must complete filing cancellation procedures (Art. 24)

Within 30 working days of receiving filing materials: National and provincial cyberspace administration departments must complete filing review and issue filing numbers or notify applicants of deficiencies (Art. 25)
penalties_summary: Violations of Articles 7, 8, 9(1), 10, 14, 16, 17, 22, 24, or 26 are punished under applicable laws and administrative regulations, or where none apply, by warnings, public reprimands, and orders to rectify within a time limit; refusal to rectify or serious circumstances incur orders to suspend information updates and fines of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000, alongside public security administration penalties or criminal liability where applicable (Art. 31). Violations of Articles 6, 9(2), 11, 13, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 27, or 28(2) are handled under relevant laws, administrative regulations, and departmental rules (Art. 32). Obtaining algorithm filing through concealment or false materials results in revocation of filing, warnings, public reprimands, and in serious cases suspension of information updates and fines of RMB 10,000 to RMB 100,000; failure to deregister or receiving severe administrative penalties such as website closure or license revocation results in cancellation of filing (Art. 33).
implementation_notes: Joint departmental regulation (Order No. 9) formulated under the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, Personal Information Protection Law, and Administrative Measures on Internet Information Services. Covers five categories of algorithm recommendation technologies: generative/synthetic, personalized push, ranking/selection, search/filtering, and dispatch/decision-making. Establishes a tiered and classified security management system (Art. 23) and is jointly interpreted by CAC, MIIT, MPS, and SAMR (Art. 34).
